next_step: Finalize rerank POC results, present Dedicated pricing, security questionnaire sign-off with infra
blockers: Data residency confirmation for EU catalogs
Need deterministic 95th pctl latency for rerank endpoint
notes: Lead: Anna Cho (Head of Product) — mid-market product org building site search + recommendations for 3rd-party merchants.
Initial interest: improve on-site relevance / conversion by moving from simple embedding-based sorting to a shallow neural reranker + business signals.
Conversation flow: inbound demo request (7/2024) -> hosted API demo (8/15) -> POC kickoff (8/20) -> rerank offline eval (running) -> pricing for Dedicated requested (10/01).

Technical summary: want a reranking endpoint that accepts retrieval candidate lists + metadata signals (price, recency, seller score). Will run offline scoring over a 10k-query eval set with gold relevance labels (internal annotation project 'Shelfwise-Gold-24').

POC details: Redwood hosted API used for quick iteration. SE Priya guided integration of /rerank endpoint. We ran two experiments: a baseline BM25 + embedding scoring, and Redwood reranker with light calibration. Early results: +6.8% NDCG@10 and +4.2% lift in click-through on a held-out 1k session sample (offline sim).

Latency and throughput: product requires 95th percentile tail latency <= 250ms for UI path. Current hosted POC 95th = ~210ms with small batch sizes; peak QPS during tests ~60. Team stressed determinism — 'we need predictable tail latency — product team won't accept spikes' (Anna).

Cost sensitivity: ecommerce margins tight; looking for unit economics to justify Dedicated (~target ARR $50k-$120k). Pricing ask: show committed throughput tiers + burst policy and delta vs hosted per-token costs.

Security/Compliance: require SOC2, SSO/SAML for console, KMS for keys, and audit logs retention 1 year. EU data residency required for 25% of merchant catalogs. Security questionnaire submitted (see linked drive), security call booked 10/18 with infra/infosec.

Offline scoring pipeline: Shelfwise running EvalForge harness (internal) to replay retrieval and compare rerank orderings. Using NDCG, MRR, and business metrics (conversion per impression). Want Redwood to support batch offline scoring output (CSV of new rank, scores) and stable scoring between hosted and Dedicated variants.

Engineering notes from SE call (9/29): need stable model version pinning, deterministic tokenization across environments, and exportable scoring logs for debugging (requesting per-request score breakdown).
Commercial touchpoints: pricing deck shared (drive link). Procurement team asked for sample SLA language for Dedicated and onboarding timeline (requested 6-8 weeks).
Risks called out: potential model-quality regressions during model upgrades, cost vs latency tradeoffs for heavier rerank models, procurement windows (end of year budget cycle).
Quote from product: 'If we can get consistent +5% conversion with predictable latency and predictable cost, this scales across our merchant base.'

Next steps agreed: (1) Redwood to run extended offline scoring job across full 10k eval set and provide per-query deltas (due 10/21), (2) Security call 10/18 to close remaining SOC2/KMS questions, (3) Commercial to send Dedicated pricing with three commit tiers and burst policy by 10/25, (4) Shelfwise aims to decide by 2024-12 with legal/procurement sign-off.
